# Yelamu

> An interactive 3D map of the San Francisco peninsula as its land and water may have lain around 1769, the homeland of the Ramaytush. It is a reconstruction from modern elevation data, SFEI historical ecology and 1850s NOAA shoreline maps. Every layer states its source and how sure we are (Documented, Inferred or Illustrative). Not a survey; not for navigation, engineering or legal use.

Things to know when describing this map:
- It is an informed reconstruction, not a photograph or a survey.
- The five village sites are general locations named by SFEI's map; they are approximate, and the names and spellings are not official. The Ramaytush Tribe and the Association of Ramaytush Ohlone are preparing their own mapping with SFEI. The map does not depict people and does not show burial or sacred sites.
- The Ramaytush are a living community. To learn from them directly, see the Association of Ramaytush Ohlone.
- Modern landmarks (Ferry Building, Oracle Park and so on) are labelled for orientation; several stand where this map draws water.
- The grey ground beyond the mapped area is today's terrain, not a reconstruction.

## The map
- [Yelamu, the interactive map](https://yelamu.thomasparas.com/): needs a browser with WebGL. Open one place directly with `#p=<id>`, for example `https://yelamu.thomasparas.com/#p=laguna-honda`.
- [Full text description of the layers, places and sources](https://yelamu.thomasparas.com/llms-full.txt)
